item.title: Mat Sadler assesses goalless stalemate with Accrington Stanley
item.description: Head Coach Mat Sadler felt that the work rate of the two sides today helped cancel each other out as Walsall played out a goalless draw with Accrington Stanley. Daniel Kanu came close in the second half with a header that clipped the crossbar, but there were very few noteworthy chances in the game. “I thought it was a tough game,” Sadler said. “Two hard working teams working very hard. item.title: Match Report: Walsall Women 0-0 Crusaders (4-2 pens)
item.description: Walsall Women advanced to the Birmingham FA County Cup Women’s Challenge Vase semi-finals with a dramatic 4-2 penalty shootout win over Crusaders Women at Dales Lane. The game ended 0-0 after 90 minutes, with neither side creating enough clear chances to win in normal time. Molly Cook, Chloe Astell and Sophie Rowlands all scored their penalties, while a combination of a stunning Olivia Wells save and Sarah Lampitt’s spot-kick sent the Saddlers through. item.description: A high-pressure match saw Walsall unable to counter in an early lead and lose out to 10 men Shrewsbury Town, reports Izaak Darvill. A threaded pass by Ellis Harris found Paul Makavore who raced into a one-on-one with goalkeeper Lewis Smart and he spread himself well to make the save. item.title: Match Report: Walsall 0-0 Crawley Town
item.description: Walsall picked up another point in their Sky Bet League Two campaign on Tuesday evening as they played out a goalless draw with Crawley Town at the Pallet-Track Bescot Stadium. item.title: Comley and Richards visit local school to feel Joy of Moving
item.description: Last week, Saddlers players Brandon Comley and Rico Richards visited the children of Old Park Primary School to get involved with their Joy of Moving session. As part of Ferrero’s corporate social responsibility programme – Joy of moving – Walsall FC Foundation host a number of sessions designed to inspire children to enjoy moving through play and to develop life-long habits which we hope will see them grow into active adults.
